{"description":"hire-attestors/src/lib.rs:66-73 declares `SignedAssertion` as `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct` with public fields and NO impl block (no `new()`, no `Default`, no builder).

`#[non_exhaustive]` on a struct forbids external crates from using struct-literal syntax entirely. `Attestor::prove()` (lib.rs:125-129) returns `Result<SignedAssertion, AttestorError>`. Therefore a third-party crate can implement `name()`, `enumerate()` and `freshness()` but physically cannot return `Ok(..)` from `prove()` — there is no expressible value of the success type. The only implementable `prove` is one that always errors, which is exactly what every in-tree attestor does today, so the gap is invisible from inside the workspace (hire-attestors/src/oidc.rs:182 builds it by struct literal because it is in-crate).

README.md:15 lists attestor plugins as a first-class extension point. As shipped, the extension point does not work off-workspace.

Fix: add `SignedAssertion::new(bytes, format)`, or drop `#[non_exhaustive]`. Same audit applies to any future non_exhaustive struct that appears in a trait method's return position.","title":"SignedAssertion cannot be constructed outside hire-attestors, so Attestor is unimplementable by third parties"}
